name: Traversal iterators close on every loop exit path

input.source_text: mut closed = 0; mut n = 0; class It { public fun next() -> Object { n = n + 1; if n < 3 { Iteration.yield(n) } else { Iteration.done } } public fun close() -> Object { closed = closed + 1; nil } } class S { public fun iterator() -> Object { It.new() } } module M { public fun natural() -> Object { mut t = 0; for x in S.new() { t = t + x }; closed } public fun broke() -> Object { for x in S.new() { break }; closed } public fun raised() -> Object { let r = try { for x in S.new() { raise :boom } } catch e { e }; [r, closed] } public fun run() -> Object { let a = natural(); n = 0; closed = 0; let b = broke(); n = 0; closed = 0; let c = raised(); [a, b, c] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. The earlier reason measured `for x in It.new()`, which is the wrong shape: C044 obtains the Iterator through the canonical Iterable protocol, so a traversal source answers `iterator()`. Measured with that shape, a programmable Iterator traverses and C046's close-on-every-exit already holds: natural exhaustion, break, return and a body exception each close exactly once, and continue stays inside the traversal so the loop closes once at exhaustion. Verified by c046_closes_a_programmable_iterator_on_every_exit_path.
